title: Spec-PTC: Speculative Parallel Test-Time Compute
brief: A write-up of Spec-PTC, a speculative parallel test-time compute framework for long-horizon agents. Interesting if you follow inference-scaling tricks for agentic workloads.
details: Speculative Programmatic Tool Calling (alexzhang13.github.io) — a 2026 blog post by Alex L. Zhang (of RLM fame) proposing a latency trick for code-action agent harnesses: speculate and pre-launch tool calls from partially generated REPL calls while tokens are still streaming, rather than waiting for the whole generation to finish. The high-level design: imported tool calls get a hook so a "shadow REPL" (a deepcopy fork of the main code REPL, with unsafe functions like `open` marked as blocked) parses the partial output and launches speculatable calls asynchronously; when the real REPL later invokes them, they resolve from a promise store. Handles literals immediately, safely-computable dependencies after evaluation, and tracks unique instances of identical non-deterministic calls. Reported gains on RLMs: generally 1-1.2x on OOLONG benchmarks (Qwen3-30B-A3B, 8xH100 vLLM). The post surveys related work (Conveyor, Speculative Interaction Agents, AsyncFC) and links the full reference implementation (github.com/alexzhang13/spec-ptc). Worth reading for anyone building code-first agent harnesses.
